perf.summary: Fortune.Build is a non-functional skeleton: it copies inputs to outputs and returns n with no Voronoi/sort logic, despite AggressiveInlining and an O(N log N) claim in comments.
perf.currentCost: Ships an inlined no-op that misleads callers (returns vertices == input points) and the [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] forces a copy loop to be inlined into every caller with zero benefit.
perf.proposedChange: Either implement the actual sweep or drop AggressiveInlining (a loop-of-n copy should never be force-inlined) and mark the method clearly as unimplemented. If kept as a passthrough, replace the manual copy loop with two Buffer.MemoryCopy calls for xs->outX and ys->outY.
perf.rationale: Buffer.MemoryCopy on blittable doubles is a single vectorized memcpy versus an element-wise scalar loop; removing AggressiveInlining avoids code-bloat at call sites for a non-hot copy.
perf.risk: MemoryCopy preserves exact bytes for the n doubles; behavior identical. Removing AggressiveInlining has no observable effect.
